name: Javier Gomez Mijangos
degree: Double Bachelor's Degree in Mathematics and Computer Science
bio: I study Mathematics and Computer Science at Université Paris-Saclay, with graduation expected in June 2028. I build interactive software and explore mathematical ideas through code. I am seeking Summer 2027 internships in software engineering, AI/ML, quantitative research, and computational research.

battle.title: Battle Tower
battle.context: Hackathon project | Programmer, team of two
battle.summary: First place at Build Sprint (BuildNXT), among 17 submitted projects. Programmer on a team of two, implementing all application features. The exercise-driven game connects camera observations to a shared progression engine; current development includes local saves and phone-camera pairing.

study.title: StudyVillage
study.summary: A hackathon project developed further into a collaborative study application. Editable notebooks and PDF annotation sit inside a Canvas village; private notes persist locally and shared pages recover after disconnection. Developed with AI-assisted coding.

bakery.title: Tiramisu Bakery
bakery.summary: A bakery storefront with guest checkout, scheduled delivery, transfer-receipt review and order administration. Includes TOTP administrator authentication and tests of order and payment workflows.

classifier.title: Utensil Image Classification
classifier.summary: University project classifying knives and spoons through foreground processing and six geometric features. Compared classical classifiers through feature distributions, balanced accuracy and confusion matrices on a small image dataset.

diffusion.title: Diffusion and Image Denoising
diffusion.summary: Independent study of an MIT generative-AI course: implemented denoising training loops and DDPM sampling using PyTorch and Hugging Face components on MNIST/Fashion-MNIST. Recorded training losses and inspected generated samples.

ray.title: C++ Ray Tracer
ray.summary: Implemented a CPU ray tracer following Ray Tracing in One Weekend. Ray-sphere intersections, randomized sampling, recursive scattering and material models produce scenes with reflections, refraction and depth of field.

battle.award.text: Won 1st place among 17 projects at Build Sprint (BuildNXT); implemented all application features as the programmer on a team of two.
battle.award.evidence: User-confirmed contribution; organizer announcement supplied by user, 15 Nov 2026. Award applies to the submitted project, not every later feature.

battle.engine.text: Separated exercise observations from game progression in a typed reducer; accepted unique events drive combat and rewards.
battle.engine.evidence: real-life-battle-tower: src/tower/engine.ts, unitReceipt.ts, model.ts; current source.

battle.vision.text: Integrated local MediaPipe pose tracking with exercise counters; retained explicit manual and assisted modes when observations cannot verify movement.
battle.vision.evidence: real-life-battle-tower: src/exercises/ExerciseCamera.tsx, src/tower/exerciseProfiles.ts; current source, not a detector-accuracy claim.

battle.saves.text: Implemented independent local save slots and revision-aware cloud command handling, with separate developer-preview state.
battle.saves.evidence: real-life-battle-tower: src/tower/useTower.ts, supabase/functions/tower-command; deployment not independently certified.

study.product.text: Developed a collaborative study application with AI-assisted coding, combining a Canvas interface, editable notebooks and PDF annotation.
study.product.evidence: studyvillage: README.md and app source; hackathon origin confirmed by user.

study.sync.text: Implemented local notebook persistence and shared-page synchronization with durable outgoing operations, revision checks and recovery after disconnection.
study.sync.evidence: studyvillage: app persistence/synchronization source and server; existing CV and README.

study.tests.text: Used app/server regression tests to check document editing and synchronization behavior; packaged the application for browser and desktop use.
study.tests.evidence: studyvillage: package.json, app/server test suites and release README; no current test-count claim.

bakery.commerce.text: Built a Django storefront with guest checkout, scheduled delivery, transfer-receipt review and order-management workflows.
bakery.commerce.evidence: tiramisubakeryProject: orders, payments, delivery, catalog, panel source; original CV contribution.

bakery.security.text: Implemented TOTP administrator authentication and tests covering order, payment and security workflows.

classifier.features.text: Built an image-processing pipeline to isolate utensils and extract six geometric features, including elongation, roundness and template-matching scores.
classifier.features.evidence: Data-Science-Spoon-knives: demo.ipynb and utilities.py; university provenance confirmed by user.

classifier.compare.text: Compared KNN, SVM, tree-based and neural-network classifiers using balanced accuracy and confusion matrices on a small knife/spoon dataset.
classifier.compare.evidence: Data-Science-Spoon-knives: demo.ipynb model list and evaluation cells; no validated accuracy claim.

classifier.limits.text: Visualized class-specific feature distributions to examine how geometric descriptors separate knives from spoons.
classifier.limits.evidence: Data-Science-Spoon-knives: demo.ipynb feature distribution histograms and feature-space scatter plot.

diffusion.training.text: Implemented denoising training loops on MNIST/Fashion-MNIST while studying an MIT course, using PyTorch and Hugging Face U-Net components.
diffusion.training.evidence: diffusion-course: DiffusionModel.ipynb, README.md; independent course context from original portfolio.

diffusion.ddpm.text: Trained noise prediction with sampled diffusion timesteps, mean-squared error and Adam; generated images through iterative DDPM denoising.
diffusion.ddpm.evidence: diffusion-course: DiffusionModel.ipynb training loop, DDPMScheduler, sampling loop.

diffusion.evaluation.text: Recorded training-loss curves and inspected generated samples to examine how the model denoises images.
diffusion.evaluation.evidence: diffusion-course: DiffusionModel.ipynb plots and outputs; no quantitative generative-quality evaluation found.

ray.geometry.text: Implemented ray-sphere intersections and recursive light scattering in C++17 while following Ray Tracing in One Weekend.

ray.sampling.text: Used randomized pixel and lens sampling to render diffuse, metal and dielectric materials with depth of field.

ray.math.text: Translated vector geometry, reflection and refraction into material models, including Schlick approximation for dielectric reflectance.
